- [S2435] types=[LIMITATION, WARNING] scope=METHODOLOGICAL — "Theta (the proposed generative knowledge-transition operator) must not be treated as an established KnowledgeOS transformation; earlier work explicitly left the operational transformation semantics (delta) unresolved, so introducing Theta as settled would jump over an existing research gate." (anchor: "We must not yet call Theta the KnowledgeOS transformation. At present it is a research hypothesis about epistemic state transition.")
- [S2435] types=[DISTINCTION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Chain of required distinctions strengthened beyond the source metaphor: Reconciliation != Closure, Closure != Determination, Determination != Knowledge, Knowledge != Truth; the pipeline becomes Proposal->Challenge->Evidence->Assessment->Reconciliation->[open question: what conditions permit a Closure Event?]->Determination->KnowledgeAttribution." (anchor: "Reconciliation != Knowledge ... Reconciliation != Closure ... Closure != Determination ... Determination != Knowledge ... Knowledge != Truth. This is absolutely necessary given everything we discovered in Experiment G.")
- [S2435] types=[COUNTEREXAMPLE] scope=OBJECT — "Negative test: when two equally authoritative, current, conflicting pieces of evidence exist, reconciliation cannot legitimately select either one -- establishing Interaction !=> Closure, ReconciliationAttempt !=> Reconciliation, and EvidenceExchange !=> Knowledge as adversarial negative principles." - [S2435] types=[CORRECTION, DEFINITION] scope=OBJECT — "Corrects the metaphor's 'offspring' concept: an epistemic interaction produces a successor epistemic state (which may contain unresolved conflict, rejected proposal, new evidence, revised determination, newly discovered boundary, or supersession), not automatically 'new knowledge' -- knowledge results only if knowledge-attribution conditions are separately satisfied." (anchor: "The 'offspring' is better understood as: the successor epistemic state, rather than automatically 'new knowledge.' ... Interaction -> {K_{t+1} if knowledge attribution conditions are satisfied; K'_{t+1} otherwise}.")
- [S2435] types=[DEFINITION, DISTINCTION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Proposes reframing Knowledge from 'a thing' to 'a temporally situated epistemic state' evolving via epistemic interaction/inquiry (K_t -> K_{t+1}), and distinguishes two different standing questions: Zero's 'what does K_t actually establish?' versus closure's 'has this inquiry reached its admissible boundary?'" (anchor: "Knowledge is a temporally situated epistemic state, whose evolution is something like K_t -[epistemic interaction / inquiry]-> K_{t+1}, with Zero continuously asking 'What does K_t actually establish?' and the closure question asking 'Has this particular inquiry reached its admissible boundary?' Those are different questions.")
- [S2437] types=[CORRECTION, CONCEPT] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Rejects Knowledge = Person_A (+) Person_B in favor of 'knowledge is generated by interaction'; a knowledge state is not merely a collection of facts but contains the history and structure of the epistemic interaction that produced its current commitments." (anchor: "The deeper interpretation is: Knowledge is generated by interaction rather than: Knowledge = A+B. ... A knowledge state therefore isn't merely a collection of facts. It contains the history and structure of epistemic interaction that produced its current commitments.")
- [S2437] types=[FORMALIZATION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Formalizes the 'intercourse of arguments' as an Interact: Proposal x Challenge -> EpistemicAssessment operator feeding K_{t+1}=Theta(K_t,Proposal,Challenge,Evidence,Assessment); reframes the metaphor as describing the generative mechanism of state change, not the content of knowledge." (anchor: "Interact: Proposal × Challenge → EpistemicAssessment. Then: K_{t+1} = Θ(K_t, Proposal, Challenge, Evidence, Assessment). ... It is describing the generative mechanism by which the state changes.")
- [S2437] types=[DEFINITION, DISTINCTION] scope=OBJECT — "Reinforces E_t != K_t: E_t is the whole argumentative/epistemic field (proposals, objections, hypotheses, evidence, uncertainty, conflicts, rejected alternatives, unresolved questions), while K_t is the current knowledge representation extracted/attributed from E_t -- only some of the field becomes attributable knowledge." (anchor: "E_t = whole argumentative/epistemic field ... K_t = current knowledge representation extracted/attributed from E_t. This is a much stronger formulation than treating every argument as knowledge.")
- [S2437] types=[FORMALIZATION, CORRECTION] scope=OBJECT — "Formalizes Offspring_t=Theta(Proposal_t,Challenge_t,Evidence_t,Assessment_t,Standards_t) merged into K_t only if state-transition rules are satisfied; explicitly rejects K_{t+1} superset-or-equal K_t as a requirement since knowledge-state evolution can be non-monotonic (new knowledge, revision, retraction, refinement, changed interpretation/context, newly discovered contradiction)." (anchor: "Offspring_t = Θ(Proposal_t, Challenge_t, Evidence_t, Assessment_t, Standards_t). Then: K_{t+1} = K_t ∪ Offspring_t only if the new result satisfies the appropriate state-transition rules. ... It does not necessarily have to be K_{t+1} ⊇ K_t ... knowledge-state evolution can be non-monotonic.")
